SECTION V - ANY PROBABLE ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS WHICH CANNOT BE AVOIDED
5.01 General. This section contains a summary of the adverse environmental effects associated with the construction, operation, and maintenance of the proposed Amistad Reservoir hydroelectric facility. It should be noted that this discussion of impacts is necessarily subjective, so no degree of importance of one impact over another is intended nor should be implied.
Probable Adverse Construction Effects
5.02 During the two to three years construction period, the influx of construction workers and their families is predicted to have brief impacts upon the surrounding communities. These impacts will probably include increases in traffic noise, air pollution, congestion, and other minor impacts. There will also be minor adverse impacts associated with the construction activities. Increased local traffic, noise levels, and air and water pollution are inevitable impacts associated with construction. Minor impacts will result from the presence of construction equipment, buildings, excavation from borrow area, and other construction activities. Certain minor adverse effects on water quality can be expected primarily in the form of sedimentation and turbidity. Wildlife can be expected to be disturbed by construction noise, dust, and human activity. Construction traffic may temporarily disrupt local traffic which may cause minor incompanies to the general public. These short-term adverse effects will be minimized by strict controls and through close supervision of construction activities.
Probable Adverse Operational Effects
5.03 Loss of Environmental Quality. During operation and maintenance of project facilities, ambient air quality is expected to decrease slightly in the immediate vicinity of the powerhouse. Noise levels will periodically rise above the background levels. Solid waste will be generated. During summer stratification, water quality immediately downstream of Amistad will be adversely affected. Even though these effects are considered only as minor impact upon the local environment, they will contribute to the overall loss of environmental quality.
5.04 Effects on Land. Hydroelectric facilities will occupy a small area which was previously excavated for this purpose. Before the riverbanks stabilize, the proposed hydroelectric releases will probably accelerate the natural phenomenon of bank sloughing. Although isolated bank sloughing is not considered a significant impact upon the land resource, it does constitute a minor adverse impact.
5.05 Effects on Vegetation. The primary impact upon vegetation will probably be from the initial bank sloughing. Although this impact is considered insignificant in itself, it does contribute to the overall loss of environmental quality.
5.06 Effects on Esthetics. The introduction of new manmade elements will slightly diminish the scenic value of the area. The switchyard, together with associated transmission lines, would cause 2 very minor disturbances to the visual landscape.
5.07 Effects on Recreation. The impact upon recreation should not be significantly different from current operations. Although the impacts upon recreation should be minimal, the slightly lower water level (on the average) at Amistad Reservoir could reduce the quality of recreation experience.
